second_order: parodying appreciation posts for April Fools
theme_note: These codes hold together the practice of moderators and members turning the familiar appreciation-post format into the subreddit’s own April Fools joke. What varies is whether people reveal and contain the parody, answer it by demanding more, or reproduce the familiar format.

second_order: working out what happened to the banner
theme_note: These codes join questions, answers, invitations to look, delight, and a navigation complaint because participants are collectively making sense of and responding to the changed banner and flair. What varies is whether they explain the date and time-zone timing, enjoy the joke, or report that it makes the subreddit harder to use.

second_order: calling Critters to put a mark on r/place
theme_note: These codes share the practice of making the canvas actionable for Critters by proposing pixel art, choosing a logo and colours, giving coordinates and links, asking for help, reporting an attempt, and revising toward a realistic goal. What varies is the proposed location, design, scale, and whether the call is an aside, a post, or a reply.

second_order: turning competing pixel attempts into one shared template
theme_note: These codes hold together the work of aligning separate pixel actions: asking for a grid, reporting tiles and a triangle, calling for more hands, disputing whose triangle it is, judging feasibility, and offering a template for the hive mind. What varies is whether a turn coordinates, reports progress, identifies confusion, or doubts the build.

second_order: making and watching a tiny tribute
theme_note: These codes form one small practice: a participant makes a separate tiny tribute, repairs it, invites others to watch it, and checks it on each pixel cooldown. What varies is creation, repair, recruitment, and repeated watching.

second_order: enforcing spoiler tags on a canvas proposal
theme_note: This single code records the subreddit’s moderator-operated practice of applying its ordinary spoiler-tag rule to an r/place proposal; it belongs with no other coded practice.

second_order: celebrating and sharing credit for finishing
theme_note: These codes hold together retrospective claims that the build was finished, intact, and a shared journey. What varies is simple congratulations, announcing the ending, vigilant credit, and an account of one person starting the Natural 20 before others completed it.

second_order: negotiating room and trading help with neighbors
theme_note: These codes share the practice of making the build possible through other groups: answering collision requests, getting permission, bringing or requesting help, thanking helpers, promising protection, accepting overlap, and talking in a communal Discord. What varies is whether the exchange concerns space, assistance, reciprocity, or compromise, and whether it happens on Reddit or is reported back from Discord.

second_order: choosing between adding more and defending what they had
theme_note: These codes hold together the recurring decision over whether to expand or preserve the existing mark and nearby helpers. What varies is proposing a d20 or another logo, exploiting open space, refusing to dig into others’ work, warning about overlap, switching to defense, telling Critters not to be greedy, and watching the finished mark closely.
